# Measured combinations

Which component works under which method, **measured**: every cell of this page is a
recorded run of [`grasppanda compose` and `grasppanda probe`](../user_guides/combinations.md),
and nothing is inferred from a contract or from another cell. The contract tables of
[Swapping components](swapping.md) say what the config check accepts; this page says
what happened when the accepted combinations were built, trained and asked to predict.

**No AP appears on this page, and none follows from it.** A probe trains 20 iterations
on 8 frames. It shows whether a combination *works*: it builds, its losses are finite,
seeds reach its head, it predicts. It says nothing about how good the combination is;
that takes a full training run and an evaluation on a benchmark split.

## What was run

- **Grid**: 208 cells (145 `runs`, 6 `runs-unstable`, 51 `refused`, 6 `fails`): every shipped method config as it is, every registered scene encoder under every seed-based method, every variant of every other stage with one stage replaced at a time, the legal sets of stage variants, and HGGD as it is. The variants of a stage are its presets plus every component whose constructor defaults no preset states.
- **A cell**: `grasppanda compose <method config> --set <slot>=<choice>`, so that an encoder is fitted and adapters are inserted exactly as a user gets them, then `grasppanda probe <composed config> --iters 20 --frames 8`: the real trainer with the method's own recipe on the split `sample` of GraspNet-1Billion (RealSense; scene 0, frames 0, 32, …, 224), then prediction on two of those frames. Both commands of every cell are in the [measured file](measured_combinations.json).
- **One exception to "as a user gets them"**: configs that read the width histogram of Scale-Balanced-Grasp were probed with the reference's own file (`scale_statistic.source: legacy_import`), because the native histogram is a statistic of the whole training split and a probe reads eight frames. The override is part of the recorded command.
- **When and where**: 208 cells on 2026-10-13 with GraspPanda at commit `e849e98`, PyTorch 2.7.1+cu118, Python 3.12.7, on one NVIDIA RTX A6000 shared with other jobs, 2 probes at a time.
- **Two cells with one config are one experiment.** A cell that composes to the very config of another cell (the same config hash) shares its probe; one that composes to its method's shipped config is marked *own*. 43 of the 208 cells share a probe.

| Group | Cells probed | `runs` | `runs-unstable` | `refused` | `fails` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `reference`: the methods as shipped | 5 of 5 | 5 | — | — | — |
| `encoder`: one scene encoder replaced | 55 of 55 | 43 | 6 | — | 6 |
| `stage`: one other stage replaced | 95 of 95 | 44 | — | 51 | — |

| **all** | **208 of 208** | **145** | **6** | **51** | **6** |

## Verdicts

| Verdict | In a table | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `runs` | ✓ · ✓ own · ✓ in `Adapter` | On real frames: the detector was built, every requested training iteration ran with finite losses and at least one real seed, the weights stayed finite, and prediction returned valid grasp groups for every probed frame. |
| `runs-unstable` | ≈ (n) | On real frames: training and prediction ran to the end, but a loss or a weight became non-finite, or an iteration had no real seed (no scene point passed the proposal, so only the proposal was trained), or no iteration supervised a seed. |
| `refused` | ✗ (n) | The config check refused the config (the same check as `grasppanda print-config --check --for train`). Nothing was built; the report carries the messages. On this page all 51 refusals come from `grasppanda compose`, which runs that check on the composed config and writes nothing when it fails. |
| `fails` | **fails** (n) | An exception was raised after the config check had passed. The report names the phase (build, data, optimizer, loss, backward, step, hook, predict), the component it came from and the message. |
| `wired` | — | No real frame was read. On a synthetic table-top scene with random labels the detector was built, back-propagated a loss through every stage and predicted. This shows that the stages connect; it says nothing about real data. Not used on this page. |

*✓ in `Adapter`*: the bare swap is refused by the contract between encoder and proposal; compose wrapped the encoder in the one adapter that bridges it, said so, and the adapted config ran. *†*: compose also fitted the encoder to the method, setting `out_channels` to the width of the encoder it replaces or `in_channels` to the point features the method feeds. *(n)* points to the reason below the table: for a refusal the first sentence of each message of the config check (the whole messages, with the fix they propose, are in the measured file), for a failure the phase, the component and the exception, for an unstable run what was unstable. *‡* marks numbers that depend on the load of a shared machine.

## Measured classes

A component **works** under a method when its cell is `runs` or `runs-unstable`: the combination was built, trained for the probe's iterations and predicted, directly or in the adapter compose inserted. The class of a component counts the seed-based methods (GSNet, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp, GraspNet-baseline, Scale-Balanced-Grasp) it works under:

- **universal**: it works under all five seed-based methods.
- **most**: it works under three or four of them.
- **some**: it works under two.
- **specific**: it works under exactly one.
- **none**: it works under none of them as it was probed.

*≈n* after a class: under n of those methods the run was `runs-unstable`; the note under the table says what was unstable. A class is a statement about this grid: these presets, the methods' own recipes, this dataset, one stage replaced at a time. A stage that is refused alone may work together with the stage it depends on (a head bundle with its assigner and its labels); those are the [sets of stages](#sets-of-stages).

### View stages

| Component | GSNet | EconomicGrasp | FineGrasp | GraspNet-baseline | Scale-Balanced-Grasp | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ObjectnessViewStage`<br>preset `objectness-view-graspable` | ✗ (1) | ✗ (2) | ✗ (2) | ✓ | ✓ own | **some** |
| `ObjectnessViewStage`<br>preset `objectness-view` | ✗ (1) | ✗ (2) | ✗ (2) | ✓ own | ✓ | **some** |
| `TemplateViewStage`<br>preset `template-view` | ✓ own | ✓ own | ✓ own | ✓ | ✗ (3) | **most** |

1. ObjectnessViewStage reads 'on_object' and 'view_width' of the matched labels, which NearestLabelAssigner returns only with `supervise: object_seeds` and `view_widths: true`. GraspnessFPS and ObjectnessViewStage both predict and supervise the 'objectness' of a seed.
2. ObjectnessViewStage computes its targets from 'dense' matched labels, but CompactLabelAssigner returns 'compact' ones. GraspnessFPS and ObjectnessViewStage both predict and supervise the 'objectness' of a seed.
3. ScaleBalancedAssigner returns a loss weight per seed, but TemplateViewStage does not apply seed weights, so the weighting would silently do nothing there. OperationHead as configured reads the seed score 'objectness' when it decodes, but neither SubsampledSeeds nor TemplateViewStage predicts it.

1. CompactLabelAssigner returns 'compact' matched labels, but SWADHead is supervised with 'dense' ones. data.train.dataset: transforms[2] (SampleGraspLabels) reads the dense label grids, which a dataset with `compact_labels` does not serve.
2. CompactLabelAssigner returns 'compact' matched labels, but OperationHead is supervised with 'dense' ones. ObjectnessViewStage computes its targets from 'dense' matched labels, but CompactLabelAssigner returns 'compact' ones. data.train.dataset: transforms[2] (SampleGraspLabels) reads the dense label grids, which a dataset with `compact_labels` does not serve.
3. NearestLabelAssigner returns 'dense' matched labels, but EconomicHead is supervised with 'compact' ones.
4. ScaleBalancedAssigner returns a loss weight per seed, but TemplateViewStage and SWADHead do not apply seed weights, so the weighting would silently do nothing there.
5. ScaleBalancedAssigner returns 'dense' matched labels, but EconomicHead is supervised with 'compact' ones. ScaleBalancedAssigner returns a loss weight per seed, but TemplateViewStage and EconomicHead do not apply seed weights, so the weighting would silently do nothing there.
6. ObjectnessViewStage reads 'on_object' and 'view_width' of the matched labels, which NearestLabelAssigner returns only with `supervise: object_seeds` and `view_widths: true`.

## Passed the check, failed afterwards

6 cell(s) passed the config check and failed afterwards. A combination should be refused with the conflict and the fix, or run; each group below is a gap between what the config check knows and what the components need. (*N* stands for a number that differs from cell to cell.)

- **at build, in the grouper DepthCylinderGroup: ValueError: DepthCylinderGroup: the gated seed residual adds N-channel seed features to N-channel crop features.** 6 cell(s): `encoder/Scale-Balanced-Grasp/LitePT`, `encoder/Scale-Balanced-Grasp/PTv3`, `encoder/Scale-Balanced-Grasp/PTv3Sonata`, `encoder/Scale-Balanced-Grasp/PTv3Utonia`, `encoder/Scale-Balanced-Grasp/PointNeXt`, `encoder/Scale-Balanced-Grasp/PointNet2Dense`.

    The message of the first, whole: *DepthCylinderGroup: the gated seed residual adds 72-channel seed features to 256-channel crop features; the two must be equal (in_channels is injected by the detector: it is the width of the scene encoder). End mlp_channels on 72, or use an encoder that returns 256 channels, or set seed_residual: none.*

    Why the check does not see it: the contract rules compare what components declare, and no contract states the width an encoder returns; it is known once the encoder is built. An encoder with an `out_channels` option does not meet the gap, because compose sets that option to the width of the encoder it replaces. The encoders above have no such option and return their own width, which this grouper cannot add to its 256-channel crops. Until a width contract closes the gap, `grasppanda probe` is what catches it, and the ways out are the three of the message.

## Not on this page

- Accuracy of any kind. See the method pages of the [model zoo](../model_zoo.md).
- Other datasets, cameras and recipes than the ones named above.
- Combinations of two or more replaced stages beyond the stage sets.
- Inner parts of HGGD: it has no registered slots yet, so it is probed as it is.

## Adding a component

A new encoder or stage appears in the grid by being registered. Give it a preset if its options cannot be guessed ([Try a combination](../user_guides/combinations.md)), probe its cells and regenerate:

```bash
python -m tools.probe_grid run --only 'encoder/*/MyEncoder' 'stage/*/*/my-preset'
python -m tools.probe_grid export
python -m tools.make_combination_docs
```

`tests/unit/test_combine_grid.py` fails until every cell of a registered component has a record in the measured file.
